title: [YouPass Collect] - Occupational distribution in Ashby versus UK average
prompt: The charts below show the percentage of people aged 23-65 in different occupations in one UK town (Ashby) and in the UK as a whole in 2008. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie charts illustrate the distribution of employment across seven occupational categories for individuals aged 23-65 in the town of Ashby compared to the entire UK in 2008.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the most notable difference was that personal service accounted for the largest proportion of workers in Ashby, while office work was the dominant sector nationally. Additionally, Ashby had considerably lower percentages of people in professional and technical occupations compared to the UK average.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the more prevalent employment sectors, personal service was the leading occupation in Ashby, representing just over one-fifth of the workforce at 21%, which was 4% higher than the national figure of 17%. Office work, meanwhile, showed relatively similar proportions in both areas, accounting for 18% in Ashby and 19% across the UK. As for shop work, Ashby's figure stood at 14%, which was slightly higher than the nationwide percentage of 13%.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Concerning the remaining occupations, professional and technical work were significantly less common in Ashby than in the UK as a whole, at 8% and 9% respectively, considerably below the national averages of 14% and 17%. Notably, technical work showed the largest discrepancy, with Ashby's rate being almost half that of the UK. In contrast, construction work made up a substantially higher proportion in Ashby at 16%, nearly double the UK's 10%. Finally, unemployment stood at 14% in Ashby, which was 4 percentage points above the national rate of 10%.
